headline: TI-New Source guidelines confirmed with corrections; certificates issued for MRL-fixed crops first; no new 9(3B) extensions while the Madras High Court status quo holds; biopesticide fast-track for registered strains; Methyl Bromide ban in Chad.

changes.d: The appeal against the 467th RC guidelines was found not maintainable. The RC kept the requirements (livestock metabolism already waived in the 468th) with some scientific corrections, and ACFI's request to go back to the 449th RC requirements was not accepted.

changes.t: Certificates for crops with fixed MRLs
changes.d: A CR is issued for the crops whose MRL FSSAI has fixed; the remaining crops are added by corrigendum/addendum on CROP once their MRLs are fixed.
Because of the Madras High Court's status quo order of 02.03.2026, extensions already granted continue but no new 9(3B) extensions are given until the writ appeals are decided.

changes.t: Biopesticides: registered strains need no fresh data
changes.d: For a strain already registered, only molecular identity from ICAR-NBAIM and quality testing at CIL are needed; steps to cut the NBAIM DNA backlog, including asking ICAR-NBAIR about extra capacity.
Chad has banned import and use of Methyl Bromide; a public notice will ask registrants to comply.
Decisions on the 12th Open House Meeting with associations (16.01.2026) are in Annexure 3.2.1.
155 files pending over 18 months for want of 1–3 experts; manpower shortage noted as the main bottleneck.

changes.t: Marketing and technical-sale questions sent to the law officer
changes.d: "Marketed by" arrangements and selling technical in other States were sent for legal examination (decided in the 472nd).

changes.t: Fake test report: Sunshine Fine Chemsol
changes.d: Reply to the show-cause notice on a forged report was considered.

actions: 9(3) applicants: expect the CR first for MRL-fixed crops, then addenda.
9(3B) registrants: no new extensions for now.
Methyl Bromide exporters: do not ship to Chad.
